html:
The Turkic migrations were the spread of Turkic peoples and languages from Mongolia across the Eurasian steppe and into Iran and Anatolia between the 6th and 11th centuries. They changed the main languages of Central Asia from Iranian to Turkic.

It began when the Türk Khaganate overthrew the Rouran in 552 and spread in every direction. When the Türk empires fell, other Turkic states took their place:

  • the Uyghur Khaganate in Mongolia, whose people later settled in the oases of Turfan and Gansu
  • the Khazars between the Caspian and the Black Sea
  • the Pechenegs and the Cumans and Kipchaks on the western steppe
  • the Kara-Khanids in Kashgar and Transoxiana

Many Turks came south as slave soldiers for Muslim rulers, then took power themselves. Others came as whole tribes. After Satuq Bughra Khan turned Muslim in the 10th century, Turkic rulers became great patrons of Islam. In the 11th century Mahmud al-Kashgari wrote a dictionary of the Turkic languages for Arabic readers.

The biggest single move came with the Seljuks, Oghuz Turks who took Iran and Baghdad in the 11th century. After their victory over the Byzantines in 1071, Turks settled in Anatolia, the land that became Turkey.

Today Turkic languages are spoken from Turkey and Azerbaijan through Central Asia to the Uyghurs of China and the Sakha of Siberia.
